main_body: Tall brick townhouse with a slate mansard roof, a dormer, a chimney, an orange cornice, three storeys of windows and a green front door
top_band: Rows 17-22 form a light grey-green roof band (L 95-122). Below it the slate roof slope runs from row 23 to about 43 (L 53-134) with a dormer. An orange cornice at rows 44-46 closes the roof, and the brick front face starts at row 48.
evidence: The roof is a large, clearly visible sloped surface of about 26 rows, with a flat roof band on top and a dormer. It sits above an orange cornice line (rows 44-45) with a dark shadow row (row 46) under it, and then the brick wall. The windows have stone surrounds and sills and the door is set in a frame, so they read as inset. The walls are front-facing, as on the Beodeul house references. The roof slope reads as the top surface, so the building passes the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The brick, slate and stone surfaces are shaded in several steps, with brick texture and lit windows, and flat-fill coverage is only 2%. However, 97% of the dark edge pixels are neutral near-black (e.g. #1d1722), which is the uniform sticker-style outline. The references use outlines tinted to the adjacent material (7-9% neutral). The candidate has 47 distinct colours against 185 and 66 for the references, and 14 colours per tile against 18 and 11, so it is thinner overall. The near-black outline is the deciding weakness.
